title: GalleryUp — Vector Art Welcome
objective: GalleryUp accepts SVG files as images. Upload one that runs script when an admin views the gallery.

verifier.condition: A gallery page embedding an uploaded SVG exfiltrates the admin-only token rendered on that page, proving script inside the SVG executed.

weakness: SVG is an XML document format that can carry a <script> element, and the gallery accepts and stores SVG uploads unmodified, then embeds them directly in a page using a tag that lets that script execute.
vulnerableEndpoint: POST /gallery/upload then GET /gallery (each stored SVG's raw markup is inlined directly into the page's own HTML)
seededData: An empty gallery to start. An admin-only token is rendered on the gallery page for admin sessions.
hints: Upload a plain, harmless SVG first (a circle or a rectangle) and see how the gallery renders it.
SVG isn't really an image format the way PNG or JPEG are — it's a full XML document. XML documents can contain more than shapes.
Look at how the gallery actually embeds each uploaded file in the page — not every embedding tag treats its content the same way.
burpNotes: Use 'Simulate admin visit' on /gallery after uploading your SVG — the exploit needs to run in a browser context, not just an HTTP request.
